negative_reviews.author: Bibi
negative_reviews.text:
The food was decent, not bad but neither impressive. But the thing that affected this whole experience the most was the way we got treated by a specific staff. Upon arrival there was no one, so we seated ourselves to an empty table. 5 to 10 minutes later a Scottish waiter came by, and without a proper hello or anything he said: you ok?? In a weird way. We initially got confused and thought it was his way of asking guests how they are, but his question got immediately followed by: who seated you? In which we just politely replied and asked if we had to wait, he then said there's a whole que and that we skipped it, we then replied that when we arrived there was no one. He looked like he didn't believe us and started questioning us. We repeatedly said that there was no que when we arrived, but he continued going on about it. Eventually I asked him what he wanted us to do, as there's no reason to go back and forth about this, he then said with an attitude "well you seated yourselves to a table thats obviously not cleaned so might as well stay" and left. We then got served by an Asian guy, who stayed polite and friendly.

I understand that it's not okay to cut a que, but that wasn't the case and the way the waiter addressed this is very shocking. This kind of behavior would absolutely not get accepted from where I'm from in EU West. This whole situation could have been handled differently, in a civilized way. I as a customer had to discuss a solution rather than a weird back and forth approach that the waiter was going for.

The next day we wanted to eat ramen again, and although this location was the most efficient for us, we decided to go out of our way to find another place.

negative_reviews.author: Ellie Bleasdale
negative_reviews.text:
Today was my 5th visit to Maki & Ramen in Leeds, having previously really enjoyed the food and brought along different friends and family on each occasion. My only previous criticism would have been how close together the tables are. Unfortunately, tonight’s experience has completely changed my opinion.

The service was extremely disappointing. We waited 15 minutes to be approached, so ended up ordering through the QR code on the table. After receiving our drinks and sharing some sushi, we waited around 35–40 minutes for our ramen. During this time, two tables who arrived after us had already received the exact same dishes. We were never asked if we wanted to order another drink either.

When we eventually asked about our order, we were told the ticket hadn’t gone through to the kitchen and asked to show our email receipt. There was no apology, and nobody had checked whether we were enjoying our starter or offered us another drink while we waited. We then waited a further 15 minutes for our food.

Having ordered the same ramen on all five visits, I was really disappointed with it. The broth was nowhere near as good as previously, and by this point the long wait and poor service had completely put me off. The only positive was that the karaage chicken was still as good as ever.

To finish things off, when we asked to take the remaining food home, we were simply handed two containers to decant the ramen into ourselves.

It’s such a shame that a restaurant I’ve previously enjoyed and recommended has left me feeling this way. Unfortunately, I won’t be returning or recommending it going forward. There are plenty of other places in Leeds serving great ramen, and the service tonight has completely put me off coming back. Unfortunately, due to us paying online we had already paid the full amount otherwise we’d have probably asked for the bill & left after the sushi. Then to finish the visit no one asked if we had enjoyed the food , apologised before we left or even said bye thanks for coming as any other restaurant would.

negative_reviews.author: Phoebe Chen
negative_reviews.text:
The servers are friendly enough and I can see they aren’t slacking at all, but management is clearly a little disorganised beginning from when you are sat down to the order and timing of the food being brought out.

We ordered 2 ramens (tonkostu ramen & steak ramen) and 1 green dragon roll which came to £55. Not much to complain about the sushi it was quite nice, but the ramen is another story. The broth was thick, heavy and oily which is basically the complete opposite of what good ramen is meant to be (light & clean). There was something off with the noodles it seemed to have a weird texture and was chewy. Perhaps it was boiled for too long? Needless to say, we didn’t finish the ramen at all and still spent £55. In the photo attached you can see the layer of oil. Maybe this restaurant is more suited to British tastes, very clearly not targeted for actual Asian palettes.

negative_reviews.author: Martina Spragg
negative_reviews.text:
Will not be returning!!!!

The time waiting for food was crazy long, other tables sat after us were served, ate and left before we got our food.

I sent back my ramen which was not hot, tepid at best. When I finally got a replacement the seafood was so overcooked especially the prawns and salmon  which had turned to unchewable rubber but were not even warm. The seafood was horrid.

Servers were like deer in headlights that didn't know what to do when I didn't want a third replacement.

negative_reviews.author: Claire “Claire Jones” Jones
negative_reviews.text:
Seems an ongoing issue but all noodles and some other bits were out of stock. Unsure why but looking at other reviews it seems this is normal for them.
Food was okay, nothing to write home about. Gyozas were nice.
Food came before our drinks which was odd.

negative_reviews.author: Shaz R.
negative_reviews.text:
I really don’t want this to come across as complaining, as I understand that not everything was within Maki Ramen’s control, especially as I ordered through Slerp.

However, the back and forth between Slerp and Maki Ramen while trying to cancel the order was exhausting, particularly after being told I couldn’t cancel.

We’ve just moved in and currently don’t have a kitchen or microwave, so waiting over an hour only to receive cold food was really upsetting, especially as I was starving. In the end, we couldn’t even eat the food, which was really disappointing given the circumstances. I appreciated receiving a full refund, and I was also grateful that a goodwill gesture was offered for the inconvenience by Chris the assistant manager, although I haven’t received any further update on this.

I’m not trying to be difficult or unappreciative, and I do understand that things can go wrong. I was just really disappointed because, after such a stressful move and currently not having a kitchen or microwave, the experience was much harder than it needed to be. Ultimately, we were left unable to eat our food after waiting over an hour, and although the refund was appreciated, it didn’t change how disappointing the overall experience was.

Looking at all the positive reviews, I don't understand whether they are all fake or whether I was just unlucky.
We entered the restaurant without a reservation, and the manager didn't seem very happy to welcome us.
